codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Implement DA trim handling instead of ignoring removals**

`mergeConfigurations` now emits `toTrimData` when `minHeight` is raised or `maxHeight` is lowered, but `DaIndexer.trimData` is an empty method, so those updates no longer remove out-of-range `DataAvailability` rows. Because DA config IDs are stable across `sinceBlock`/`untilBlock` edits, stale rows for the same `configurationId` remain queryable and can leak into DA aggregates after a config window change.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Process EigenDA layer trim requests to avoid stale records**

This indexer now receives trim diffs for configuration window changes, but `trimData` is a no-op, so reducing the active range does not delete previously indexed rows for that `configurationId`. After changing `sinceTimestamp`/`untilTimestamp` with a stable config ID, old `DataAvailability` rows remain and can be returned by repository time-range queries.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Apply trim cleanup for EigenDA project configurations**

Like the layer indexer, this class leaves `trimData` empty even though the new merge flow emits trim operations for range-narrowing config updates. When project DA tracking windows are tightened without changing `configurationId`, old rows are never deleted, so historical data outside the new bounds can still affect downstream reads.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Preserve progress when trimming raised minHeight**

When `c.minHeight > stored.minHeight`, this branch always sets `currentHeight` to `null` after trimming only the lower slice. That makes the indexer restart from the new `minHeight` while rows in `[c.minHeight, oldCurrentHeight]` are still present, so tracked-txs reprocessing will reinsert existing rows and can fail on unique keys because `LivenessRepository.insertMany` and `L2CostRepository.insertMany` do plain inserts (no upsert/conflict handling). Keep `currentHeight` if it remains inside the retained range, or wipe the full config before resetting it.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Restore wipe-and-reset path for non-trimmable indexers**

This unconditional `toTrimData` path regresses the old `configurationsTrimmingDisabled` behavior: `DaIndexer`, `EigenDaLayerIndexer`, and `EigenDaProjectsIndexer` now implement `trimData()` by calling `wipeData()`, so a min/max range change can delete **all** rows for a configuration while `currentHeight` is still kept near its previous value. In that scenario (e.g. `currentHeight=1000`, `minHeight` raised to `200`), initialization marks the config as already synced and subsequent updates start after 1000, so wiped history is never backfilled. Previously this case forced `currentHeight = null` via the trimming-disabled branch.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Don’t auto-disable trimming for all indexers without trimData**

Passing `!this.isTrimDataImplemented()` into `mergeConfigurations` makes every indexer without `trimData` run in trimming-disabled mode, which can emit duplicate wipe entries when both `minHeight` and `maxHeight` change in one rollout. `DaBeatPricesIndexer.wipeData` still asserts a single removal input, so this now throws during initialization for that configuration-change shape and blocks the indexer from starting. This regression is introduced by the new auto-detection path rather than per-indexer opt-in behavior.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Update privacy indexers to the wipe/trim contract**

When the backend is built with the privacy module, this new abstract method requires every `ManagedMultiIndexer` subclass to implement `wipeData`. The privacy indexers still only override `removeData` and import the removed `RemovalConfiguration` type, so `PrivacyPriceIndexer`, `PrivacyBlockTimestampIndexer`, and `PrivacyFlowIndexer` no longer satisfy the base class and the backend build fails; migrate them to `wipeData`/`trimData` along with the other indexers.

issue.title: Visibility into events to .capture method of interop plugins
issue.description: Currently, plugins expose data requests to inform exactly which events and what context they require to be captured. As of now, it only is taken into account when plugins are resyncing. When we're following the tip of the chain, all events and full context is always sent to capture methods of plugins. This is very inefficient, and either only the requested events and requested context should be sent to the plugin, or at least much less than is sent right now. We're assuming it's still fine to send a bit more due to the simplicity of such approach, but ultimately, in the future, we will need to make it so that only exact requests are being provided to the capture method.

**Defer log-query initialization until configs are loaded**

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

**Analyze groups with zero current transfers**

Iterating only over `groupedTransfers.values()` limits checks to groups that have at least one transfer in the current snapshot. When a previously active route drops to zero activity, `aggregate()` emits no candidate row, so this path never fetches history for that group and the drop is silently missed. Since drops are part of the z-score logic, this creates a monitoring blind spot exactly for full outages; include recent historical groups in the candidate set and treat missing current groups as zero-valued candidates.

**Isolate anomaly-analysis failures from aggregation writes**

codexFindings.body:
**Do not round the next flow update past an hour**

In the UIF code I checked, child updates are invoked with `from = state.height + 1`; after this indexer returns a day boundary such as `00:00:00`, the next run starts at `00:00:01` and these lines round that up to `01:00:00`. That means the logs for `00:00:01` through `00:59:59` are never included in any `getLogs` range, so each daily chunk permanently misses the first hour of privacy activity.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Delete flow data by timestamp, not block number**

When a privacy flow configuration is trimmed, updated, or deleted, `RemovalConfiguration.from`/`to` are timestamp heights because this indexer advances by Unix timestamps, but this repository method compares them to `blockNumber`. On Ethereum those timestamp values are around 1.7B while block numbers are around tens of millions, so config changes/deletions will leave the old flow events in the database and the dashboard can continue aggregating stale rows.

codexFindings.body:
**Align highlight metrics to one comparison window**

This method fetches three independent “latest” timestamps (`aggregatedInteropTransfer`, `activity`, `tvsTokenValue`) and later combines them into one highlights payload, so the cards can compare values from different 24h windows whenever one pipeline lags or advances. In practice this makes cross-metric statements misleading (e.g. interop inflow at `T` vs UOPS/TVS at `T-1d`). Use a single reference snapshot timestamp (or enforce timestamp equality and omit mismatched sections) before assembling the response.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Filter UOPS increase to interop chains only**

The UOPS delta query is built from the entire `Activity` table with no interop scope filter, so any non-interop project with a large daily change can be surfaced as the interop highlight. Because this powers an interop insights endpoint, the result set should be constrained to the interop chain/project IDs; otherwise the metric is semantically incorrect for this dashboard.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Filter TVS increase to interop chains only**

The TVS delta query also scans all projects in `TokenValue` and groups by `projectId` without any interop filter, so the reported “largest TVS increase” can come from projects unrelated to interop. Since this value is exposed in interop highlights, it should be restricted to the same interop project universe to avoid showing unrelated chains.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Resolve prior snapshot by availability before computing deltas**

The volume-delta highlights use `latestTimestamp - 24h` and fetch that exact timestamp, but interop aggregation intentionally skips hours when syncers are behind, so the exact prior timestamp can be missing even when nearby historical data exists. In that case `previousInteropRecords` is empty and the calculators treat previous volume as `0`, producing inflated “largest increase” results rather than a valid day-over-day comparison. This should use the latest available snapshot at or before the target comparison time (or return no delta when unavailable) before calculating chain/token/protocol increases.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Filter UOPS/TVS highlights by configured interop chains**

This router hard-codes `INTEROP_CHAINS` for the project filter instead of using the configured chain set passed through router dependencies. When deployments enable only a subset of interop capture chains, UOPS/TVS highlights can be computed from chains that are not enabled in that environment, making the highlights inconsistent with the rest of the dashboard data scope.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Filter activity timestamp lookup to interop projects**

When any non-interop activity project has a newer snapshot than the configured interop chains, this global `getMaxTimestampAtOrBefore` chooses that day and the later UOPS calculation filters the fetched rows down to `interopProjects`. In that scenario the UOPS highlight can report no positive delta even though the interop chains have valid data at their own latest day. Pick the max activity timestamp from the configured project ids before fetching current/previous/older rows.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Filter TVS timestamp lookup to interop projects**

TVS value indexers run per project, so if an unrelated TVS project is ahead, this global max timestamp can select a snapshot where the configured interop projects have no rows yet; after `getLargestTvsIncrease` filters by `interopProjects`, the TVS card will show no delta despite valid interop TVS data at an older timestamp. The timestamp lookup should be scoped to the configured interop project ids before loading the current/previous/older snapshots.

humanComments.author: torztomasz
humanComments.body:
Thermo-nuclear code-quality pass. Two correctness bugs (collectOutgoingFields, onDoubleClick wrapper), one hot-path perf regression, a boundary leak, and one structural theme worth deciding on before this calcifies. Details inline.

**Structural theme (no single line):** a group is a `Node` with nested `subnodes`, but nearly every consumer needs a *flattened* view, so the diff hand-rolls ~14 different recursions over the same tree (`selectedLeafIds`, `collectIds`, `collectAllIds`, `topLevelByDescendant`, `collectDragPositions`, `shiftSubnodes`, `indexSubnodes`, `toggleOpened`, `translateNode`, `expand`, `indexDescendants`, the walks in `buildStoredNodeLayout`/`reconstructGroups`, `snapshotNodesEqual`). The persisted model is already flat (`StoredGroup.members: string[]`) and the rendered model is flat — only the in-memory model is nested, and it's the sole source of all this recursion. Minimum: extract `walkTree`/`mapTree`/`flattenLeaves` primitives and express the walkers in terms of them. Worth considering: a flat `nodes` + `groups` map so drag/selection/storage reuse the existing flat machinery.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Resolve selected subnodes when syncing panels**

When a child inside an opened group is clicked or box-selected, `selectedNodes` contains that child's id, but the child is no longer present in the top-level `nodes` array after grouping. This filter therefore produces an empty `selectedAddresses` list, so the global selection is not updated and panels like Values/List/Preview keep showing the previous contract even though the node is visibly selected.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Keep every external edge on collapsed groups**

When a grouped contract has more than one field pointing outside the group, the first external field adds `node.name` to `seen`, so every later external field from the same contract is skipped even if it targets a different node. The collapsed group then omits real connections, and the layout buttons operate on an incomplete dependency graph for grouped nodes with multiple outbound references.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Compare nested nodes for undo snapshots**

When a member inside an opened group is dragged, `shiftSubnodes` changes only the nested `subnodes` tree while the parent group's top-level id/name/color/box/hiddenFields can remain unchanged. `wrapHistoryEndAction` relies on this equality check, so it treats that drag as a no-op and discards the pending snapshot, leaving undo/redo unable to restore member moves inside opened groups.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Honor hidden members while expanding groups**

When a member inside an opened group is selected and Hide/Delete is used, `hidden` contains that member id, but the render graph only filters top-level nodes before expansion. This `flatMap` then emits every subnode regardless of `hidden`, so hidden group members keep rendering and remain selectable until the whole parent group is hidden.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Preserve all outgoing edges when grouping**

When a selected contract has two outgoing fields to different external contracts, this de-duplication key is just the source node name, so every outgoing edge after the first is dropped from the collapsed group. The group view then hides dependencies for that member (and also drops edges from different members that share the same display name); de-duplication needs to include the target and/or field identity rather than only `node.name`.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Preserve groups across project-data reloads**

Because `useLoadNodes` clears the node store and rebuilds every API entry with `subnodes: []` here, the synthetic `group:*` nodes created by `groupSelected` are not reconstructed from `ApiProjectResponse` or the saved layout. After any project data reload/remount, existing user-created groups are discarded, and the next layout persist can also lose the grouped members' prior locations. Reconcile the existing group tree or persist groups before replacing the node state.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Migrate the persisted selected value to an array**

Changing `selected` from `string | undefined` to `string[]` without a persist migration leaves existing `discovery-app-selection-store-v1` localStorage entries rehydrating as a string. In that state, code such as `state.selected[0]` reads the first character of the address and the app restores or focuses the wrong contract until the selection is overwritten. Add a persist version/migration or normalize the value on rehydrate.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Restore groups when applying saved layouts**

Saving/exporting now writes `groups`, but the layout manager's Load/Import path calls `applyStoredLayout`, which only maps `saved.locations`, `colors`, `hiddenFields`, and `hiddenNodes` onto the current flat `state.nodes` and never consumes `saved.groups`. As a result, a layout saved with groups reloads ungrouped from the committed/imported layout flow, making v4 layout files lossy outside the localStorage recall path. Please reconstruct the group tree when applying a stored layout.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Handle nested selections when grouping**

When a group is opened, mouse hit-testing can put member ids into `state.selected`, but those members are nested under their parent and are no longer present in top-level `state.nodes`. Filtering only this top-level array makes Alt+G/the Group button no-op for selections inside an opened group, and mixed top-level+nested selections silently drop the nested members. The grouping operation needs to walk and update the node tree, not just top-level nodes.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Avoid sending nested nodes to the resize path**

Because `graph.nodes` includes members of opened groups, this hit-test can start a resize with `resizingNode` set to a nested member id. The resize handler still looks up the node with `state.nodes.find(...)`, so it cannot find nested members and dragging their resize handle silently does nothing. Either look up/update nested nodes in the resize path or exclude them from resize hit-testing.

**Handle decimal-string durations in FormatSeconds**

When a call or storage read returns an integer above the safe-number range, discovery normalizes it to a decimal string before edits run (`toContractValue` returns `value.toString()` for large `BigNumber`s, and `bytes32ToContractValue` does the same for large storage numbers). codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Validate URL envs against own keys**

For malformed deep links such as `?env=toString`, the `in` operator accepts inherited `Object.prototype` properties, so `readEnvironmentFromUrl()` returns a non-environment value and `setEnvironment` persists it for the current session. On the next render `ENVIRONMENTS[environment]` resolves to that inherited function instead of falling back, and consumers like the environment banner dereference `config.classNames`, crashing the backoffice page. Check own keys only, e.g. via `Object.hasOwn(ENVIRONMENTS, value)`.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Reset the promotion scroll guard per hash target**

When a user follows one promotion deep link and then navigates to another hash while this page stays mounted, `scrolledRef.current` remains `true`, so the effect returns before scrolling the newly requested snapshot into view. The highlight changes because it uses `highlightTimestamp`, but the viewport remains on the old row; track the last scrolled timestamp instead of a boolean, or reset the ref when the hash changes.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Ignore unsupported URL environments**

When the hosted backoffice is opened with `?env=local` (for example from a local backend alert link), this effect writes `local` even though production builds omit `ENVIRONMENTS.local`. On the next render `useBackendTrpc()` selects `CLIENTS.local`, but `TRPCReactProvider` only mounts the local `PinnedProvider` when `urls.local` exists (`packages/backoffice/src/react-query/trpc.tsx:62`), so interop pages render without a matching local TRPC provider instead of falling back. Please ignore URL environments that are not present in `ENVIRONMENTS` (or avoid emitting local links).

issue.description:
To count mined Aztec L2 transactions, count transaction effects in blocks (this counts both public and private txs).

Each block returned by `node_getBlocks` includes `body.txEffects` when called with

transaction, so the transaction count for a block range is:

```js
sum(block.body.txEffects.length)
```

Get the latest block number:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://aztec.rpc \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"node_getBlockNumber","params":[],"id":1}'
```

Count the transaction effects:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://aztec.rpc \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"node_getBlocks","params":[64800,50,{"includeTransactions":true}],"id":2}' \
  | jq '[.result[].body.txEffects | length] | add'
```

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Keep Aztec activity batches under the RPC cap**

When Aztec activity catches up by at least 50 heights, `BlockActivityIndexer.update()` calls the count service with an inclusive range ending at `from + batchSize`, and `AztecActivityBlockProvider` converts that to `node_getBlocks(start, to - from + 1)`. With `batchSize: 50`, that becomes a 51-block Aztec RPC request, exceeding the documented 50-block limit and leaving the activity indexer retrying without progress. Set this to 49 or change the batching semantics so the Aztec request never exceeds 50 blocks.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Use the aztec_* RPC namespace**

Aztec v5/mainnet exposes public node RPC methods under `aztec_*`, not `node_*` (see the [Aztec migration notes](https://docs.aztec.network/developers/docs/resources/migration_notes#node-json-rpc-method-prefixes-changed-to-aztec_-and-aztecadmin_)), so with the configured mainnet dRPC endpoint this call and `node_getBlockNumber` above will get a JSON-RPC method-not-found response and the activity target/count indexers will keep retrying instead of indexing Aztec activity. Please switch these method names to `aztec_getBlocks`/`aztec_getBlockNumber`.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Query a stable Aztec tip for activity**

When Aztec has proposed blocks that are not yet checkpointed/proven, calling `aztec_getBlockNumber` without a chain-tip selector lets the timestamp search target the proposed tip, and the range fetch below can then persist counts for blocks that may still be pruned. Since `BlockTargetIndexer` rejects later decreases in block height, those provisional counts can either leave over-counted activity or stall the indexer once the proposed tip is replaced; please request a stable tip such as `checkpointed`/`proven` consistently for both the target lookup and block fetches.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Use the Aztec node RPC method names**

When this client is used with the newly configured dRPC/Aztec node endpoint, these `aztec_*` methods are not part of the exposed Aztec RPC surface; dRPC lists `node_getBlockNumber`/`node_getBlocks`, and the Aztec node RPC reference says node methods use the `node_` prefix ([docs](https://docs.aztec.network/operate/operators/reference/node_api_reference)). As a result the target lookup and block batch requests will get method-not-found errors and Aztec activity will never index until both constants are switched to `node_getBlockNumber`/`node_getBlocks`.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Use a stable Aztec tip for activity targets**

When Aztec has unproven proposed blocks, calling `aztec_getBlockNumber` with no chain-tip argument uses the latest/proposed tip, so `BlockTargetIndexer` can persist activity targets for blocks that may later be pruned. In that scenario the follow-up `getBlocks` calls can either count transactions for a block range that disappears or get stuck retrying on incomplete ranges; activity should target a stable tip such as `proven`/`finalized` instead of the default.

issue.description: [https://github.com/l2beat/l2beat/pull/12303](<https://github.com/l2beat/l2beat/pull/12303>)

humanComments.author: torztomasz
humanComments.body:
`getLivenessGroupingKey` throws on calldata that doesn't ABI-decode, and this path matches raw block txs by `to` + 4-byte selector only — no receipt/success check. Anyone can send a cheap reverting tx to the Rollup address with selector `0x069d1525` and garbage calldata: the decode throws, `matchLivenessTransactions` rejects, and `BlockIndexer` catches it at the processor level — so the **whole block is skipped** for `RealTimeLivenessProcessor`: all projects' real-time liveness matching *and* the `checkForAnomalies` call for that block are silently lost (just a `Processor failed` log). Repeatable for ~21k gas per block.

The batch path is safe (the Dune query filters `tr.success = true`, so the contract itself already decoded any calldata we see), but here please wrap the key extraction in a try/catch and drop the record on failure — a call the contract couldn't decode isn't a real proof, so skipping it is also semantically correct.

project.name: Project compare page
project.summary: Universal project-comparison chart page at /scaling/compare: pick up to 10 projects, switch metric (TVS, activity), absolute/indexed modes, fully shareable URLs.
project.description:
## Problem Statement

L2BEAT shows rich aggregate charts on every metric page (TVS, activity, costs, …) and per-project charts on each project page, but there is no way to see two or more projects on the same chart. A user asking "is Base catching up to Arbitrum?" or "which ZK rollup grew fastest this quarter?" has to open multiple project pages side by side, eyeball differently-scaled axes, or export data to an external tool. Comparison — one of the most common analytical questions about the scaling ecosystem — is the one thing the site can't answer directly.

## Solution

A new first-class page, `/scaling/compare`, where the user picks up to 10 scaling projects and sees them as overlaid line series on a single chart. The metric is a switchable dimension of the page (TVS and activity at launch), not a separate destination — switching metric keeps the selected projects. An indexed view mode rebases every series to 100 at the start of the range so projects of wildly different size can be compared on growth. Every piece of chart state lives in the URL, so a shared link reproduces the exact chart the sender saw. The page is reachable from the sidebar, from "Compare projects" buttons on the metric pages, and from "Compare" links on project pages that seed the selection with that project.

## User Stories

 1. As a visitor, I want to select several scaling projects and see their TVS as overlaid lines on one chart, so that I can compare them directly instead of flipping between project pages.
 2. As a visitor landing on the compare page with no selection, I want to immediately see the top 5 projects by the active metric, so that the page demonstrates its value without any setup.
 3. As a visitor, I want to search projects by name in a picker that shows project logos, so that I can build my selection quickly and confidently.
 4. As a visitor, I want my current selection shown as removable chips, so that I can prune the comparison at a glance.
 5. As a visitor trying to add an 11th project, I want a friendly "remove one to add another" message instead of a silent failure, so that I understand the limit.
 6. As a visitor, I want to switch the metric (TVS ↔ activity) while keeping my selected projects, range, and view mode, so that I can examine the same cohort from multiple angles.
 7. As an analyst, I want an indexed view that rebases every series to 100 at the start of the range, so that I can compare growth rates between projects of very different size.
 8. As an analyst, I want a logarithmic scale option in absolute view, so that large and small projects remain readable on one axis.
 9. As a visitor, I want to change the time range, so that I can compare projects over the window that matters to me.
10. As a content creator, I want to share a URL that reproduces my exact chart (projects, metric, range, mode, scale, toggles), so that my audience sees the same insight I saw.
11. As a visitor, I want browser back/forward to step through my previous chart configurations, so that exploring feels like normal web navigation.
12. As an analyst, I want a USD/ETH unit toggle on the TVS metric, so that I can strip out fiat price action from the comparison.
13. As an analyst, I want an "exclude associated tokens" toggle on the TVS metric, so that a project's own token doesn't distort the comparison.
14. As an analyst, I want the RWA-restricted-tokens display control on the TVS metric, so that compare numbers always match the TVS page.
15. As an analyst, I want a UOPS/TPS toggle on the activity metric, so that I can compare activity in the unit I think in.
16. As a visitor, I want a "Show Ethereum" baseline on the activity metric, rendered as a visually distinct dashed series, so that I can benchmark L2s against L1 without Ethereum occupying a selection slot.
17. As a visitor, I want to temporarily hide a series by clicking its legend entry, so that I can focus the chart without rebuilding my selection.
18. As a visitor, I want the tooltip to list projects sorted by value with their logos, so that I can read a crowded timestamp at a glance.
19. As a visitor on the TVS or activity page, I want a "Compare projects" button next to the chart, so that I can jump into a comparison with the right metric pre-selected.
20. As a visitor on a project page, I want a "Compare" link on its TVS and activity sections, so that I can start a comparison seeded with that project.
21. As a visitor, I want a "Compare" entry in the Scaling navigation, so that I can discover the feature without hunting for buttons.
22. As a mobile visitor, I want the picker to open as a full-screen sheet and the chart and controls to remain usable, so that comparison isn't a desktop-only feature.
23. As an analyst comparing a range that predates a project's launch, I want its indexed series rebased at its first data point with a tooltip note, so that I'm not misled by partial data.
24. As a visitor opening a shared link, I want the chart server-rendered with data prefetched from the URL, so that I don't watch loaders before seeing the insight.
25. As an L2BEAT developer, I want new metrics to be addable as registry entries without touching the route or page shell, so that costs, liveness, and DA comparisons ship cheaply later.
26. As an L2BEAT operator, I want the entire feature gated behind a feature flag, so that it can be deployed, tested, and rolled back independently of a release.

## Implementation Decisions

* **Feature flag.** Everything ships behind the `FEATURE_FLAG_COMPARE_PROJECTS` environment variable, added to the frontend's validated env schema as a boolean defaulting to `false` (following the existing coerced-boolean flag pattern). When the flag is off: the `/scaling/compare` route is not served (404), and every entry point — sidebar item, metric-page buttons, project-page links — is hidden. The flag is established in the tracer-bullet ticket and respected by every subsequent ticket; launch is flipping the flag, and the flag is removed once the feature is considered stable.
* **Single destination.** One route (`/scaling/compare`) with the metric as a switchable dimension. Explicitly rejected: per-metric sub-routes (`/scaling/tvs/compare`, …) and an in-place compare mode on existing pages.
* **Metric registry.** Each metric declares its label, data query, series extractor, unit options, per-metric controls, Ethereum-baseline support, and top-N default ranking. The page shell contains no metric-specific conditionals; v1 registers TVS and activity, later metrics are new entries only.
* **Chart semantics.** Overlaid lines, never stacked. Two view modes: absolute (with linear/log scale) and indexed (every series rebased to 100 at range start, computed client-side from already-fetched data, metric-agnostic; scale toggle hidden in indexed mode; index values shown unitless).
* **URL is the source of truth** for all chart state: metric, projects (as slugs, not ids), range, mode, scale, and every per-metric control, with defaults omitted for clean links. SSR prefetches chart data from the URL params via the existing tRPC helper flow.
* **Data contracts.** TVS reuses the existing per-project-series endpoint (which honors per-project since/until ranges and the associated-tokens/RWA params). Activity gets one new tRPC procedure returning one series per project for a project-id set and range, mirroring the TVS endpoint's shape and its batching/caching approach (cost profile is N projects × full-range reads). Existing aggregate endpoints are untouched.
* **Selection rules.** Live scaling projects only (rollups, validiums & optimiums, others); no archived, no upcoming. Hard cap of 10, enforced in the picker with a graceful state. Unknown or invalid slugs in the URL are dropped silently. Zero valid selections falls back to top 5 by the active metric.
* **Ethereum is not a project.** It never appears in the picker and doesn't consume a cap slot; it's a per-metric baseline overlay toggle, rendered only where data exists (activity in v1). This keeps any selection valid across every metric switch.
* **Visual system.** Per-project colors from the existing accessible color generation; interactive legend with per-series toggling; tooltip sorted by value with project logos; styled loading and no-data states; global milestones intentionally omitted; mobile picker as a full-screen sheet.
* **Entry points.** Scaling sidebar entry, "Compare projects" buttons beside the chart controls on the TVS and activity pages (metric preset), and "Compare" links on project detail TVS/activity sections (project pre-selected). All entry links emit clean URLs with defaults omitted.

## Testing Decisions

Good tests here exercise external behavior at existing seams — inputs in, observable outputs out — never component internals or render trees. Three seams, highest available:

* **The new activity per-project-series feature function** (the unit behind the tRPC procedure): given repository records for a set of projects and a range, it returns the expected per-project series. Repository mocks are typed against the database interface per repo convention (`mockObject` as `Database['repo']`), matching the existing chart-data feature tests as prior art.
* **The URL state codec**: a pure parse/serialize pair for compare-page state. Round-trip tests (state → URL → state), default-omission tests, and garbage-tolerance tests (unknown slugs, invalid enum values). Prior art: the interop pages' selection-from-search-params parsing.
* **The indexed rebase transform**: a pure function from fetched series to indexed series. Tests cover rebase-at-range-start, rebase-at-first-data-point for mid-range launches, and null-gap handling.

The registry, page shell, and picker are verified through the acceptance criteria on their tickets (demoable behavior), not through new frontend test infrastructure.

## Out of Scope

* Costs, liveness, and DA throughput metrics (the registry is designed for them; they are follow-up registry entries).
* Table-row checkbox selection ("select rows → compare") on list pages.
* Archived and upcoming projects in the picker.
* Ethereum as a selectable project, and Ethereum baseline for metrics without L1 data (e.g. TVS).
* Market-share view mode (share-of-ecosystem denominator).
* Milestones on the compare chart.
* Social preview (OG image) generation for shared compare links.
* Any changes to existing aggregate chart endpoints or pages beyond adding entry-point buttons/links.

## Further Notes

* The full decision history (10 resolved design questions) comes from a grilling session on 2026-07-29; the "do not relitigate" constraints are restated in each ticket.
* The work is broken into 7 tracer-bullet tickets in this project: L2B-14545 (tracer bullet, sole frontier ticket) → L2B-14546 (picker), L2B-14547 (indexed mode), L2B-14548 (TVS control parity), L2B-14549 (activity metric + switcher) in parallel → L2B-14550 (Ethereum overlay) → L2B-14551 (entry points + navigation, deliberately last so the feature isn't broadly exposed until the picker and both metrics exist).
* Because everything is flag-gated, tickets can merge to main continuously with `FEATURE_FLAG_COMPARE_PROJECTS` off in production; enable it in preview/staging environments for verification.
* Watch the new activity endpoint's cost profile in production; it should adopt whatever caching the TVS ranges endpoint uses rather than inventing a new strategy.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Do not price every unconfigured native token as ETH**

`getTokensOnChain` reaches this fallback on any supported chain whose token list lacks an address-less native entry, not only ETH-based chains. For example, Polygon PoS has only addressed tokens in `packages/config/src/tokens/generated.json`, so selecting a `matic:` account makes `getNativeBalance()` read its POL balance while `getTvl()` prices and labels it using the hard-coded Ethereum metadata; BSC and other custom-gas chains behave similarly. This can overstate the displayed TVL by orders of magnitude, so the native asset metadata must be resolved per chain or omitted when unknown.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Accept or skip tokens without CoinGecko IDs**

`AbstractTokenRecord.coingeckoId` is explicitly nullable, and `abstractTokens.getAllWithDeployedTokens` returns every abstract token, including unpriced records with `coingeckoId: null`. When even one such record exists, this `v.string()` rejects the entire batch response, so `fetchTokens()` throws and every TVL request returns 500. Parse the nullable field and omit records that cannot be priced instead of invalidating the complete token list.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Report failed sweeps instead of claiming the project holds no value**

When every address request fails—for example because the token-backend credential or an RPC is unavailable—failed queries are no longer pending, so `swept === holders.length` while `holdings` is empty. This branch then reports “No value held by this project” and returns before the summary can expose the failure count, misrepresenting an unavailable estimate as a successful zero result. Handle `failed > 0` separately before showing the no-value state.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Exclude tokens marked as having unreliable prices**

When TokenDB sets `isPriceUnreliable`, this schema drops that field and `parseTokens` still sends the token through CoinGecko valuation, allowing a deliberately untrusted price to inflate both the address total and treemap. The repository's financials path explicitly omits valuation for this case in `InteropFinancialsLoop.ts:294-299`; preserve the flag here and skip or leave these balances unpriced.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Exclude the configured 0x1 burn address**

Projects using `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001` as an irreversible burn sink are still treated as holding its balances. For example, the reachable dYdX discovery explicitly identifies this address as `BURN_ADDRESS` in `packages/config/src/projects/dydx/discovered.json:724`, so any tokens burned there become a dominant project holding despite the invariant documented immediately above this list. Include this known burn address, or derive burn sinks rather than limiting the filter to zero and dead.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Exclude the configured EigenLayer burn address**

Fresh evidence after the `0x1` fix is `packages/config/src/projects/shared-eigenlayer/discovered.json:7,2548`, where reachable EOA `eth:0x00000000000000000000000000000000000E16E4` is explicitly identified as `DEFAULT_BURN_ADDRESS`. Because it is absent from this list, projects referencing shared EigenLayer still sweep and value tokens sent there, potentially letting burned balances dominate the treemap despite the invariant documented above the list; exclude this configured sink or derive burn addresses from discovery data.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Give same-ticker token rows unique keys**

When an address holds multiple token contracts with the same ticker, these rows receive duplicate React keys, so refetching or reordering the response can cause React to reuse or remove the wrong row and display stale token values. This is a supported data case—the repository already contains two distinct Ethereum `mETH` contracts in `packages/config/src/tokens/generated.json:3702-3728`—so the API should expose a token identifier/address and use it as the key rather than `ticker`.

**Preserve whitespace in the selected symbol**

When a genuine conflict involves a deployed or custom symbol with leading/trailing whitespace (for example, `wBEPE ` versus `BEPE`), this unconditional trim silently writes a different abstract-token symbol than the researcher selected. **Prevent concurrent resolve submissions**

When a researcher double-clicks Resolve within `ButtonWithSpinner`'s 150 ms loading-state debounce, both calls enter this function because there is no synchronous in-flight guard. Each call generates a different token ID, and abstract tokens do not have a uniqueness constraint on `coingeckoId`, so both plans can execute successfully and create duplicate abstract tokens for the same coin; subsequent `findByCoingeckoId` lookups can then select either record. Disable submission immediately or guard the handler with a ref before starting the first mutation.

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Keep the dialog open while resolution is running**

When a researcher presses Cancel, Escape, or the backdrop after starting resolution, this handler immediately closes and unmounts the dialog, but the pending `generatePlan`, `executePlan`, and retry promises continue running. The abstract token can therefore be created despite the apparent cancellation, and the researcher may repeat the action and create a duplicate; ignore close requests and disable Cancel while `isResolving` is true.

**Dead links in "Used in" badges.** `getContractUtils()` builds the "Used in" hrefs via `getProjectUrl`, which has no `defiInfo` branch (and `getContractUtils` doesn't select `defiInfo`), so DeFi projects fall through to `/scaling/projects/<slug>`.

Fix: add a `defiInfo → /defi/projects/<slug>` branch to `getProjectUrl.ts` and add `'defiInfo'` to the `optional` select in `getContractUtils.ts`.

humanComments.author: torztomasz
humanComments.body:
Table TVL sums each token's **last non-zero** `valueForProject` (`getLastNonZeroValueByProjects` filters `value > 0` per `(project, token)`), while the project-page chart (`getTvsChartByProjects` → `getSummedByProjectForRanges`) sums all tokens at each timestamp. The two can disagree: if a collateral pool is fully drained, the newest rETH row is `0` (zero rows are persisted by `TokenValueIndexer`) and gets excluded, so the table keeps adding the stale last non-zero value while the chart's latest point already excludes it — and the table mixes tokens from different timestamps (see `TokenValueRepository.test.ts:487-509`).

Same convention as `getPrivacySummaryEntries`, so pre-existing, but if table and chart should agree, summing the latest per-project timestamp via `getSummedByProjectForRanges` (as `get7dTvsBreakdown` does) would match.

humanComments.author: torztomasz

entries.title: Don't crash refresh-discovery on project failure
entries.author: mateuszradomski

humanComments.author: torztomasz

codexFindings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
codexFindings.body:
**Preserve a failing exit status after processing projects**

When any project rejects, this catch records the error but allows the command handler to resolve normally after the summary, so `l2b refresh-discovery` exits with status 0 even though one or more discoveries remain stale or partially updated. This makes shell scripts and CI treat a failed batch as successful; continue processing the remaining projects, but set `process.exitCode` or otherwise signal failure after the loop.
